prompt: I'm selling on Shopify and want to start offering product bundles to lift my average order value. Customers buy single products today; if I bundle related products with a discount I think I can get them to add more to the cart. I should be able to create and manage bundles myself from the Shopify admin — no developer help needed once it's set up. Two bundle types matter. Fixed: I pick the exact products and the customer buys the whole pack or nothing. Flexible: I define a pool and a count ("pick any 3 from this list") and the customer chooses which items they want. Each bundle should let me pick products or specific variants. The discount should be configurable per bundle. I want to choose between three discount kinds: percentage off the bundle total, a flat amount off, or buy-X-get-Y-free where one of the items is effectively included free. On top of that I want tiered discounts — the more items in the bundle the bigger the cut. For example 2 items 10% off, 3 items 20% off, 4 items 30% off. On the storefront the bundle UI should appear on the product page itself. The customer picks their items (for flexible bundles), sees the discounted total live, and adds the whole bundle to cart in one click — discount applied automatically at checkout. In the admin I want a table of all my bundles, edit any field, enable/disable per bundle, and a count of times each was bought.

intent.desiredOutcome: Merchants create fixed and flexible product bundles with global tiered discounts; customers pick items on the storefront, see live totals, and add to cart with automatic discount applied at checkout.
intent.qualityBrief: A polished bundle app handles variant selection (not just products), ensures the customer's chosen items map exactly to real Shopify line items in the cart (no virtual wrapping or relabeling), and gracefully handles product deletions / out-of-stock items in the bundle pool. The widget must show live-updating totals as selections change, with clear feedback on which tier discount applies. The admin page must let merchants reorder bundle items, bulk-enable/disable, and export purchase history. Edge cases: partial bundle purchase (customer removes an item from cart post-add), deleted products mid-bundle, inventory changes mid-selection, and duplicate discount application on refresh. The tiered rule must clamp correctly (e.g., 5 items gets the highest tier, not an error).

plan.dataFlow: The merchant builds a bundle in the admin panel — choosing fixed or flexible type, picking products or specific variants, setting a discount kind (percentage, flat amount, or buy-X-get-Y-free) with optional item-count tiers, and enabling it. Saving a bundle persists its definition and items, then creates or updates a matching automatic app discount in Shopify whose function-configuration encodes the bundle's products/variants and discount/tier rules so the cut applies automatically at checkout. On a product page the storefront widget loads that product's bundle definition, fetches live variant prices and availability, lets the customer select items (for flexible bundles), shows the discounted total and the active tier live, and adds the chosen real variants to the cart in one click. When an order is paid, the system attributes it to the bundle whose discount was applied and records a purchase-history row, incrementing that bundle's bought count. When a product is deleted in Shopify, any bundle items referencing it are flagged so the merchant and widget can react.

triggers.idempotency: if a purchase-history row already exists for the order external id, treat the event as a no-op and do not re-increment any bundle's bought count

triggers.event: a product referenced by a bundle is deleted
triggers.idempotency: flagging an already-flagged bundle item as deleted is naturally idempotent; re-delivery for the same product external id is a no-op

persistence.name: bundles
persistence.purpose: Stores each bundle's definition: type, discount configuration, status, the backing automatic discount, and its lifetime bought count.

columns.name: bundle_type
columns.purpose: fixed (whole pack or nothing) or flexible (pick N from pool)

columns.name: anchor_product_external_id
columns.purpose: the storefront product whose page hosts this bundle widget

columns.name: required_item_count
columns.purpose: for flexible bundles, how many items the customer must pick

columns.name: discount_kind
columns.purpose: percentage, flat amount, or buy-X-get-Y-free

columns.name: discount_ratio
columns.purpose: fractional discount (0–1) used when discount_kind is percentage; null for flat-amount or buy-X-get-Y-free bundles

columns.name: discount_amount
columns.purpose: flat monetary discount used when discount_kind is flat amount; null for percentage or buy-X-get-Y-free bundles

columns.name: discount_external_id
columns.purpose: the Shopify automatic app discount node that applies this bundle's cut at checkout

columns.name: discount_title
columns.purpose: the unique title given to the backing discount, used to attribute paid orders back to this bundle

columns.name: bought_count
columns.purpose: lifetime number of attributed paid orders for this bundle

queryPatterns: all bundles filtered by enabled status, ordered by most recent, cursor-paginated
single bundle by id for editing
enabled bundle by anchor product external id for the widget
bundle by discount title to attribute a paid order

persistence.name: bundle_items
persistence.purpose: The products or specific variants that make up a bundle (the fixed pack members or the flexible pool), with display ordering and a deletion flag.

columns.name: bundle_id
columns.purpose: the bundle this item belongs to

columns.name: product_external_id
columns.purpose: the Shopify product chosen for this item

columns.name: variant_external_id
columns.purpose: a specific variant when the merchant picked one rather than the whole product

columns.name: position
columns.purpose: merchant-defined display order within the bundle

columns.name: is_deleted_in_shopify
columns.purpose: set when the product-deleted event fires for this item's product so the widget and admin can react

queryPatterns: all items for a bundle ordered by position
items referencing a given product external id (to flag on product deletion)

persistence.name: bundle_discount_tiers
persistence.purpose: Tiered discount rules for a bundle: the larger the picked item count, the bigger the cut.

columns.name: bundle_id
columns.purpose: the bundle these tiers belong to

columns.name: min_item_count
columns.purpose: minimum number of items at which this tier's discount applies

columns.name: discount_ratio
columns.purpose: fractional discount (0–1) for this tier when the bundle's discount_kind is percentage; null for flat-amount tiers

columns.name: discount_amount
columns.purpose: flat monetary discount for this tier when the bundle's discount_kind is flat amount; null for percentage tiers

queryPatterns: all tiers for a bundle ordered by min_item_count ascending to clamp a selection to the highest qualifying tier

persistence.name: bundle_purchases

columns.name: bundle_id

columns.name: order_external_id

externalContracts.purpose: Return a paginated list of all bundles with type, status, discount summary, and bought count for the admin table.
Return a single bundle's full definition including its ordered items and discount tiers for the edit form.
Create or update a bundle definition, its items and ordering, and its discount/tier configuration.
Enable or disable one or more bundles in bulk, toggling their backing automatic discount accordingly.
Return a paginated purchase-history log for a bundle so the merchant can review or export attributed orders.
Return the enabled bundle definition for a given storefront product, including its items, discount kind, and tiers, for the product-page widget to render.
Given the customer's selected items, validate the selection against the bundle rule and return the discounted total and the active tier.

edgeCases: Duplicate orders/paid delivery for the same order — the existing purchase-history row by order external id makes attribution a no-op and prevents double-counting the bought count.
Duplicate products/delete delivery — re-flagging already-deleted bundle items is idempotent and changes nothing.

A bundle item's product is deleted mid-selection — the widget's live availability fetch hides it and the quote endpoint rejects selections that include it, while the is_deleted_in_shopify flag warns the merchant in admin (item availability and price are never served from a stale stored copy).
An item goes out of stock between page load and add-to-cart — the live availability fetch and the quote validation block adding the unavailable variant rather than relying on a cached flag.
A flexible selection exceeds the highest configured tier (e.g. 5 items when tiers stop at 4) — the tier resolver clamps to the highest qualifying tier instead of erroring.

A customer removes one item from the cart after adding the bundle — the automatic checkout discount only applies when the bundle's required items are present, so a partial cart simply receives no bundle discount rather than a malformed one.
Saving a bundle but the discount sync to Shopify fails — the bundle is persisted but left disabled with no discount external id so it is not shown live until the merchant retries the sync.

hld_v_findings.issue: op: "productVariants" is not a recognised Shopify Admin GraphQL operation. The spec requires every shopifySteps op to be resolved via the catalog tools; this name appears to have been composed from memory. The coding agent will attempt to call a non-existent operation and get a compile/runtime error, silently breaking the admin item-picker flow.
hld_v_findings.fix: Run get_shopify_op on the correct op for fetching variant details by id — the standard Admin API approach is either the "nodes" query (accepts an array of variant GIDs) or "productVariant" (single id); resolve the exact op name and signature from the catalog tool before emitting, and update shopifySteps accordingly.

hld_v_findings.issue: shopifySteps lists "discountAutomaticAppCreate" (step 0) and "discountAutomaticAppUpdate" (step 1) as an ordered sequential pipeline — the spec defines a multi-step list as one where "each step names what it produces and what the next step consumes." These two ops are conditional alternatives (create when no discount_external_id exists, update when one does), never both executed in sequence. Presenting them as a pipeline will mislead the coding agent into always calling both, which would create a new discount AND then attempt to update it, producing duplicate discounts on every bundle save.
hld_v_findings.fix: Split sync-bundle-discount into two separate capabilities — "create-bundle-discount" (single step: discountAutomaticAppCreate) and "update-bundle-discount" (single step: discountAutomaticAppUpdate) — or document the branching intent in the capability description and list only one step per branch, letting the coding agent choose by the presence of discount_external_id.

hld_v_findings.issue: Both the bundles.discount_value column and bundle_discount_tiers.discount_value column declare role: "ratio", but their purposes explicitly state they can hold "a flat amount depending on discount_kind" / "the discount fraction or amount granted at this tier". The spec defines ratio as "fractional values bounded between 0 and 1"; a flat monetary discount amount is unbounded and is a money role. Using ratio for money prevents the platform's money helper from applying correct minor-unit math on flat-amount discounts, and the column type the coding agent picks (e.g. REAL/DECIMAL vs. INTEGER cents) will be wrong for monetary values.
hld_v_findings.fix: Either split discount_value into two columns — discount_ratio (role: ratio, nullable) and discount_amount (role: money, nullable) — with exactly one populated per discount_kind, or document that the column always stores a ratio (0–1) and flat amounts are stored in a separate column; update both tables and any capability that reads these columns.

hld_v_findings.issue: get-bundle-for-edit (description: "Return a single bundle's full definition … for the admin edit form") and get-bundle-for-product (description: "Return the enabled bundle definition … for a given storefront product") both declare returnsList: true. The spec states returnsList must be set true when "the capability shows multiple records they can browse, sort, filter, or paginate" — both capabilities return a single bundle object (with nested item/tier lists). Setting returnsList: true incorrectly binds both capabilities to the paginate helper, which the coding agent will apply to the top-level bundle response rather than to the nested item/tier collections, breaking single-record fetch routes.
hld_v_findings.fix: Set returnsList: false on both get-bundle-for-edit and get-bundle-for-product; remove "page cursor" from their dataNeeds; if the nested items/tiers lists need pagination, handle that in the contract's requestShape (cursor already declared there) without flagging the parent capability as a list.
